mean: in a complete mess; all over the place
lit: messy sevens and rotten eights: things scattered every which way

use.how: An adjective: predicate, complement after 得 (弄得乱七八糟) or before 的. Said of rooms, writing, things or one's thoughts being in disorder.

near.diff: 一塌糊涂 stresses how bad a result or situation is (考得一塌糊涂); 乱七八糟 stresses disorder and lack of arrangement.

cue: You come home to find your teenager's clothes on the floor, books on the bed and dirty dishes on the desk. How do you describe the room?

ctx.s: 你的房间怎么{乱七八糟}的？快收拾一下。
ctx.en: Why is your room such a mess? Tidy it up.

ctx.s: 孩子们走了以后，客厅被弄得{乱七八糟}。
ctx.en: After the children left, the living room was a total mess.

ctx.s: 他的字写得{乱七八糟}，老师根本看不懂。
ctx.en: His handwriting is all over the place; the teacher can't read it at all.

ctx.s: 抽屉里塞满了{乱七八糟}的东西，找把剪刀都难。
ctx.en: The drawer is stuffed with all sorts of junk; even finding a pair of scissors is hard.

ctx.s: 这份报告的数据{乱七八糟}，你得重新整理一遍。
ctx.en: The data in this report are a mess; you need to reorganise them.

ctx.s: 最近事情太多，我心里{乱七八糟}的，什么都想不清楚。
ctx.en: So much has been going on lately; my head is in a muddle and I can't think straight.

bad.s: 弟弟昨天{乱七八糟}了我的房间。
bad.en: (meant: my brother messed up my room yesterday)
bad.why: It is an adjective, not a verb; you need a pattern like 'made my room messy' (ba ... nong de ...).

bad.s: 这家餐厅的菜种类很多，{乱七八糟}，我很喜欢。
bad.en: (meant: this restaurant has a wide variety of dishes, which I like)
bad.why: It means a disorderly mess and is a complaint; it cannot praise a wide choice of dishes.

lit: one mould, one shape: as if cast from the same mould

use.how: Predicate or attribute, usually in A跟B一模一样. Said of looks, objects, voices or events that cannot be told apart.

near.diff: 如出一辙 is bookish and compares methods or events, often critically; 一模一样 is everyday and mostly about how things look or sound.

cue: Twin sisters turn up at a party in the same dress with the same haircut, and nobody can tell which is which.

ctx.s: 这对双胞胎长得{一模一样}，我总是认错。
ctx.en: The twins look exactly alike; I always mix them up.

ctx.s: 你的手机跟我的{一模一样}，连颜色都相同。
ctx.en: Your phone is identical to mine, even the colour.

ctx.s: 他画的这只猫和照片上的{一模一样}。
ctx.en: The cat he drew looks exactly like the one in the photo.

ctx.s: “你看，这道题跟昨天考的{一模一样}吧？”
ctx.en: "Look, this question is exactly the same as the one in yesterday's exam, isn't it?"

ctx.s: 二十年过去了，这条老街跟我小时候{一模一样}，一点儿没变。
ctx.en: Twenty years on, this old street is exactly as it was when I was a child; it hasn't changed a bit.

ctx.s: 他说话的语气跟他父亲{一模一样}。
ctx.en: The way he talks is exactly like his father.

bad.s: 这两件衣服有点儿{一模一样}。
bad.en: (meant: these two pieces of clothing are a bit alike)
bad.why: It means completely identical, so it cannot be softened with 'a bit' (you dian er); for partial likeness say 'look a bit alike'.

bad.s: 他{一模一样}他爸爸。
bad.en: (meant: he looks just like his dad)
bad.why: It cannot take an object; the pattern is 'A gen B (zhang de) yi mu yi yang'.

mean: baffling; making no sense at all
lit: no one can name its mystery: nobody can say what is behind it

use.how: Predicate (我觉得莫名其妙), adverbial with 地 (莫名其妙地关机了) or an exclamation. Said of behaviour, events or words with no apparent reason.

near.diff: 不知所措 is not knowing what to do; 莫名其妙 is not understanding why something happened or what it means.

cue: Your friend suddenly gets angry at you over lunch and walks out without a word, and you have no idea why.

ctx.s: 他突然生气了，我觉得{莫名其妙}。
ctx.en: He suddenly got angry, and I was completely baffled.

ctx.s: 你这话说得{莫名其妙}，我听不懂。
ctx.en: What you just said makes no sense; I don't follow.

ctx.s: 手机{莫名其妙}地关机了，怎么也打不开。
ctx.en: My phone switched itself off for no reason and won't turn back on.

ctx.s: 大家都在笑，只有他一脸{莫名其妙}。
ctx.en: Everyone was laughing; only he looked completely lost.

ctx.s: 这条规定真是{莫名其妙}，谁也说不出它有什么用。
ctx.en: This rule is absurd; nobody can say what it's for.

ctx.s: “你干吗瞪我？”“{莫名其妙}，我什么时候瞪你了？”
ctx.en: "Why are you glaring at me?" "What are you on about? When did I glare at you?"

bad.s: 这本小说写得太好了，真是{莫名其妙}！
bad.en: (meant: this novel is so well written, it's simply wonderful)
bad.why: The 'miao' here is not 'wonderful': the idiom means baffling and cannot praise anything.

bad.s: 我{莫名其妙}这件事。
bad.en: (meant: I don't understand this matter)
bad.why: It cannot take an object; say instead that the matter leaves you baffled.

mean: have a good trip (wish to someone setting off)
lit: a following wind all the way

use.how: A farewell wish, alone or after 祝你, said to someone about to leave on a journey.

near.diff: Both are farewells; 一路平安 wishes a safe journey, 一路顺风 a smooth one.

cue: Your friend is leaving tomorrow on a long train journey home. What do you say as you see them off at the station?

ctx.s: 明天你就要出发了，祝你{一路顺风}！
ctx.en: You're setting off tomorrow. Have a good trip!

ctx.s: “我走了，到了给你打电话。”“好，{一路顺风}！”
ctx.en: "I'm off, I'll call you when I get there." "OK, have a good trip!"

ctx.s: 同事们在火车站跟他告别，祝他{一路顺风}。
ctx.en: His colleagues said goodbye to him at the station and wished him a good journey.

ctx.s: 客人们上了大巴，酒店经理在门口挥手说：“祝各位{一路顺风}！”
ctx.en: The guests got on the coach, and the hotel manager waved from the door: "Have a good journey, everyone!"

ctx.s: 妈妈把他送到车站，嘱咐了半天，最后说了句“{一路顺风}”。
ctx.en: His mother saw him to the station, gave him advice for ages, and finally said "have a good trip".

ctx.s: 你们开车回老家，路上慢点儿，{一路顺风}。
ctx.en: You're driving back to your hometown, so take it easy on the road. Have a good journey.

bad.s: 欢迎回来！{一路顺风}！
bad.en: (meant: welcome back, I hope your trip went well)
bad.why: It is said to someone leaving, not arriving; to someone who has just arrived you acknowledge the tiring journey.

bad.s: 祝你生日快乐，{一路顺风}！
bad.en: (meant: happy birthday, all the best)
bad.why: It wishes a good journey only; it is not a general good-luck wish for a birthday.

lit: self speaks, self talks: speaking with no one else to hear

use.how: An intransitive verb phrase or adverbial before 道 or a quote. Describes someone speaking aloud with no listener.

near.diff: 喃喃自语 is literary and stresses a low, murmuring voice; 自言自语 is everyday and only says there is no listener.

cue: Alone in the kitchen, your grandmother keeps saying aloud "now where did I put the salt?" though no one is there to answer.

ctx.s: 他一边做饭一边{自言自语}。
ctx.en: He talks to himself while he cooks.

ctx.s: 你一个人在那儿{自言自语}，没事吧？
ctx.en: You're over there talking to yourself. Are you all right?

ctx.s: 老人坐在窗前{自言自语}，好像在跟老朋友聊天。
ctx.en: The old man sat by the window talking to himself, as if chatting with an old friend.

ctx.s: 她{自言自语}道：“明天一定会更好。”
ctx.en: "Tomorrow will be better," she said to herself.

ctx.s: 小孩子玩玩具时经常{自言自语}，这很正常。
ctx.en: Young children often talk to themselves while playing with toys; that's perfectly normal.

ctx.s: 有人觉得{自言自语}是压力大的表现，其实不一定。
ctx.en: Some people think talking to yourself is a sign of stress, but that's not necessarily so.

bad.s: 面试开始了，请你先{自言自语}一下。
bad.en: (meant: the interview is starting, please introduce yourself first)
bad.why: It means talking with no listener, not talking about oneself; an interview calls for a self-introduction.

bad.s: 我们俩在咖啡馆{自言自语}了一下午。
bad.en: (meant: the two of us chatted in the café all afternoon)
bad.why: Two people talking to each other are chatting, not talking to themselves.

lit: wild talk and eight kinds of rambling

use.how: Verb phrase or predicate (别胡说八道, 完全是胡说八道). A blunt rebuttal of what someone says; too rude for polite or formal settings.

near.diff: 胡言乱语 is incoherent raving, as in a fever or when drunk; 胡说八道 denies that what someone claims is true.

cue: A coworker loudly claims you broke the printer, though you were on holiday all that week. You snap back at him.

ctx.s: 别{胡说八道}了，我根本没说过那种话！
ctx.en: Stop talking rubbish, I never said anything of the sort!

ctx.s: 他明明什么都不懂，还在那儿{胡说八道}。
ctx.en: He clearly knows nothing about it, yet there he is spouting nonsense.

ctx.s: 网上那些{胡说八道}的消息，你千万别信。
ctx.en: Don't believe any of that nonsense going around online.

ctx.s: “听说你要辞职了？”“谁在{胡说八道}？没有的事。”
ctx.en: "I hear you're quitting?" "Who's spreading that rubbish? It's not true."

ctx.s: 这篇文章完全是{胡说八道}，一点儿根据都没有。
ctx.en: This article is pure nonsense, without a shred of evidence.

ctx.s: 小孩子{胡说八道}，您别往心里去。
ctx.en: The child is just talking nonsense; please don't take it to heart.

bad.s: 王教授在会上{胡说八道}了一个很有意思的观点。
bad.en: (meant: Professor Wang put forward an interesting view at the meeting)
bad.why: It is a blunt insult, never neutral 'say'; it cannot describe putting forward a good idea, and is rude about a professor.

bad.s: 他在背后{胡说八道}我。
bad.en: (meant: he spread lies about me behind my back)
bad.why: It takes no object; you cannot use it to mean spreading lies about a person.

mean: to achieve two aims with one action

story.text: Bian Zhuangzi wanted to kill a tiger, but a servant boy stopped him: two tigers were about to eat an ox, they would fight over it, the smaller would be killed and the larger wounded. If he waited and then killed the wounded one, one action would win him the fame of killing two tigers. He waited, and it happened just so.
story.source: 《史记·张仪列传》（陈轸讲给秦惠王的故事）

use.how: Predicate, often after 真是 or 可谓, or before 的. Approves of one plan or action that brings two benefits at once.

near.diff: 一箭双雕 often describes a calculated move that hits two targets, sometimes against people; 一举两得 is plain approval of a practical choice.

cue: By walking the dog every morning, she gets her own exercise and keeps the dog happy at the same time.

ctx.s: 骑自行车上班，既能锻炼身体，又能省钱，真是{一举两得}。
ctx.en: Cycling to work keeps you fit and saves money: two birds with one stone.

ctx.s: 你帮我练英语，我帮你练中文，这不是{一举两得}吗？
ctx.en: You help me with my English and I help you with your Chinese. Doesn't that work for both of us?

ctx.s: 周末去做志愿者，既帮了别人，又学到了东西，{一举两得}。
ctx.en: Volunteering at weekends helps others and teaches you things too: a double gain.

ctx.s: 把旧仓库改成咖啡馆，既省了拆除费，又多了收入，可谓{一举两得}。
ctx.en: Turning the old warehouse into a café saves the cost of demolition and brings in income: a move that pays off twice.

ctx.s: 听说出差时能顺便看望父母，她觉得{一举两得}，马上答应了。
ctx.en: When she heard the business trip would let her visit her parents too, she thought it was ideal and agreed at once.

ctx.s: 有没有{一举两得}的办法，既不加班，又能按时完成？
ctx.en: Is there a way to kill two birds with one stone: no overtime, and still finish on time?

bad.s: 他先学了英语，后来又学了法语，真是{一举两得}。
bad.en: (meant: he learned English and then French, so he gained two languages)
bad.why: Two separate efforts are not one action with two results; the idiom needs a single act that brings both gains.

bad.s: 我想{一举两得}这个问题。
bad.en: (meant: I want to solve this problem in one go)
bad.why: It takes no object and does not mean 'solve'; it describes a plan or method, not what you do to a problem.

lit: to stop halfway along the road

story.text: Yue Yangzi left home to study with a teacher but came back after a year because he missed home. His wife took a knife to the cloth on her loom and said that it had been woven thread by thread, and cutting it now would waste it all; stopping his studies halfway was the same. He went back and studied for seven years without returning. The phrase itself is older, from the Doctrine of the Mean.
story.source: 《后汉书·列女传·乐羊子妻》；词语见《礼记·中庸》

use.how: Intransitive predicate, never with an object; the subject is the quitter or the undertaking (他总是半途而废, 项目半途而废). Said of studies, plans and projects.

near.diff: 前功尽弃 stresses that all earlier effort is wasted; 半途而废 stresses quitting before the end.

cue: He trained hard for a marathon for a month, then quit with the race still eight weeks away.

ctx.s: 学外语最怕{半途而废}，每天坚持一点儿就好。
ctx.en: The worst thing in learning a language is giving up halfway; just keep at it a little every day.

ctx.s: 你已经练了三个月了，现在放弃不就{半途而废}了吗？
ctx.en: You've practised for three months. If you give up now, won't you have quit halfway?

ctx.s: 由于资金不足，这个项目不得不{半途而废}。
ctx.en: For lack of funds, the project had to be abandoned halfway.

ctx.s: “我不想学钢琴了。”“做事不能{半途而废}，至少把这首曲子学完。”
ctx.en: "I don't want to learn piano any more." "You can't give up halfway. At least finish learning this piece."

ctx.s: 他减肥总是{半途而废}，坚持不到一个星期。
ctx.en: His diets always fizzle out; he never lasts a week.

ctx.s: 老师在毕业典礼上提醒我们：无论做什么，都不要{半途而废}。
ctx.en: At the graduation ceremony our teacher reminded us: whatever you do, don't give up halfway.

bad.s: 我们走到{半途而废}的地方，休息了一下。
bad.en: (meant: we stopped for a rest at the halfway point)
bad.why: It means abandoning an undertaking, not the midpoint of a route; for that just say 'halfway' (yi ban).

bad.s: 他去年{半途而废}了大学学业。
bad.en: (meant: last year he dropped out of university)
bad.why: It takes no object; say instead that he gave up his studies halfway, with the studies or the person as subject.

use.how: Adverbial, often 不知不觉中 or 不知不觉就. Said of time passing or a change happening without one noticing.

near.diff: 潜移默化 is a gradual influence on someone's thinking or character; 不知不觉 is anything happening unnoticed, most often time passing.

cue: You sit down to check your phone for a minute, and when you look up it is dark outside.

ctx.s: 我们聊得很开心，{不知不觉}天就黑了。
ctx.en: We were having such a good chat that it got dark before we knew it.

ctx.s: 他躺在床上看书，{不知不觉}睡着了。
ctx.en: He was reading in bed and drifted off to sleep without realising.

ctx.s: {不知不觉}中，我来中国已经三年了。
ctx.en: Before I knew it, I had been in China for three years.

ctx.s: 跟中国朋友在一起久了，我的口音也{不知不觉}地变了。
ctx.en: After spending so long with Chinese friends, my accent has changed without my noticing.

ctx.s: 你有没有发现，孩子们{不知不觉}就长大了？
ctx.en: Have you noticed how the children have grown up before we realised it?

ctx.s: 逛街的时候，钱{不知不觉}就花光了。
ctx.en: When you go shopping, the money is gone before you know it.

bad.s: 我{不知不觉}这个消息。
bad.en: (meant: I didn't know about this news)
bad.why: It is an adverbial about not noticing, not a verb meaning 'not know'; here you simply need 'did not know'.

bad.s: 她是一个{不知不觉}的人，从来不关心别人。
bad.en: (meant: she is an oblivious person who never cares about others)
bad.why: It describes how something happens, not a person's character; it cannot label someone as oblivious.

use.how: Adverbial (一心一意地做…) or predicate after 对… (对他一心一意). Said of sustained devotion to one task, goal or person.

near.diff: 全心全意 is more formal and often about serving people or a cause; 一心一意 is everyday and also used of loyalty to one partner.
专心致志 is full concentration on the task in front of you; 一心一意 is devotion to one aim, kept up over time.

cue: After years of juggling three jobs, she quits two of them to put all her energy into the one bakery she loves.

ctx.s: 他现在{一心一意}准备考试，别的事都不管。
ctx.en: He is now devoting himself entirely to preparing for the exam and ignoring everything else.

ctx.s: 她对丈夫{一心一意}，几十年从没变过。
ctx.en: She has been completely devoted to her husband, unchanged for decades.

ctx.s: 只要你{一心一意}地做好一件事，就一定会有收获。
ctx.en: As long as you put your whole heart into doing one thing well, you will get something out of it.

ctx.s: 退休以后，爷爷{一心一意}地照顾他的花园。
ctx.en: Since retiring, Grandpa has devoted himself wholeheartedly to his garden.

ctx.s: “你真的想好了吗？”“想好了，我就想{一心一意}地画画。”
ctx.en: "Have you really thought it through?" "I have. I just want to give myself completely to painting."

ctx.s: 这家小店的老板{一心一意}做面条，十年只卖这一样。
ctx.en: The owner of this little shop has devoted himself to noodles, selling nothing else for ten years.

bad.s: 我对这份工作很{一心一意}。
bad.en: (meant: I am very devoted to this job)
bad.why: It cannot be modified by 'very' (hen); use it bare, as a predicate or as an adverbial before the verb.

bad.s: 他{一心一意}地看了一眼手表。
bad.en: (meant: he glanced attentively at his watch)
bad.why: It describes devotion kept up over time, not one brief glance; for close attention use 'carefully' (ren zhen).
